notes.content: The Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry ( Link ) is a rigorous and contemporary curriculum that is responsive to future developments, reflecting the interdisciplinary nature and diversity of the chemical sciences, thus enabling students to become successful professionals, scholars, scientifically literate citizens and leaders.
notes.contentHtml: The Bachelor of Arts in Chemistry (Link) is a rigorous and contemporary curriculum that is responsive to future developments, reflecting the interdisciplinary nature and diversity of the chemical sciences, thus enabling students to become successful professionals, scholars, scientifically literate citizens and leaders.

notes.content: (120 UNITS) The curriculum provides a strong background in the fundamental areas of chemistry and also in biochemistry. Special emphasis is placed on an authentic research experience, preparing students for scientific careers, science education, advanced degrees (M.S., Ph.D.) or professional programs. The degree is commonly pursued by students interested in pre-professional programs (e.g., forensic science, business administration, law), those interested in teaching careers and alternatives in chemistry. In addition to the requirements for the major, students must meet all other university requirements for a bachelor’s degree. Please consult the Graduation Requirements for the Bachelor’s Degree section in this catalog for complete information. The Emphasis in Environmental Chemistry may be integrated with the B.A. in Chemistry or the B.S. in Chemistry by using the courses below to meet career breadth, elective and research requirements. The courses also may be used to satisfy requirements for the minor in Chemistry. Effective Fall 2023: Biology, Chemistry and Physics LAB courses must be in-person. A combination lecture (online) and lab (in-person) course can be accepted. Please use the Articulation Details section to review course combination equivalencies. All MATH courses proposed for articulation must have in-person proctored exams, as stated in the course outline or syllabus.
